Graveyard Shift: Midnight Golf

Nine holes of real golf on a haunted course, at midnight, on your phone.

A portrait-mode golf game for phones, played in the browser. You aim, pull back with one finger and let go: she swings, the ball flies through a Halloween night, and you play the hole out. Every hole is a different haunted place: a pumpkin patch, a witch's hollow, a forgotten cemetery, a spider wood, a harvest farm, a ghost-lit marsh, a vampire's garden, the Headless Horseman's trail, and a midnight homecoming.

  • 9 holes, par 36, 3,264 yd
  • Phone, portrait, one finger
  • Plays in the browser
  • Godot 4.5
  • Holes built in Blender
  • Art direction and music by Marc
Play it: midnight-golf-wheat.vercel.app

How it plays

You start at the clubhouse, a chalkboard in a wooden hut: Play Now (the round from hole 1), Pick a Hole, Pick your Ball, Options and How to Play. Each page is wiped with a felt eraser and chalked on line by line, with chalk sounds.

A shot, start to finish

Each hole opens with a short flyover: the camera starts close on the tee's lantern as lightning cracks, pulls back to her, rises and flies down the hole to the flag while the lights along it come on one by one. A tap skips it.

These screenshots are from the game's own test bot playing hole 1 in the current build.

The course

Nine holes, par 36: two par 3s, five par 4s, two par 5s. Each hole was designed from one of Marc's concept paintings and has a safe route and a risky one (carry the trouble for a shorter next shot). Each has its own dominant tree, so every hole looks different, and its own wind range.

Balance

The numbers are real golf numbers, scaled for a short-hitting player, and every hole was checked against them (where a drive lands, how wide the fairway is there, what's left for the second shot).

Putterby the pull

The game picks the shortest club whose full swing covers the shot with 10% to spare, so most shots want 80–90% of a full pull. A button steps down the bag.

Other rules

  • Plays-like: each metre of climb plays about a metre longer.
  • Wind: random direction each hole, strength within the hole's range (up to 13 mph). The preview shows its drift.
  • Landings: drives skip and run (~9% more), irons roll a few metres, wedges stop, and on greens irons and wedges can check and spin back.
  • Putting: a full pull is twice the putt's length. The cup is drawn 1.8× real size and is forgiving: a slow ball over it drops.
  • Pace: the ball flies at 1.25× speed, easing to real time when it lands.

Design rules the holes follow

  • Wide landing areas where drives finish: about 40–50 yards.
  • Hazards at real size and irregular shapes, not circles.
  • Varied bends: three left, three right, hole 8 straight with a split fairway.
  • Slopes checked like a real course: fairways mostly under 9%, greens under 4%, gentle pond banks.
  • Trees stand back where drives land; landmark trees and buildings frame the greens.

Cards

"Card" means two things in this project.

The scorecard

After each hole a chalk card names the result (eagle, birdie, par, bogey and so on) with the strokes against par, then Next hole or Clubhouse. The round is nine holes, par 36.

Painted cards (2D art)

Trees, plants and lights are Marc's paintings, drawn on flat "cards" that always turn to face the camera, thousands per hole. It's the cheap way for a phone to draw a forest. Glowing ones (lantern ghosts, grave candles, skull lanterns) also throw light on the ground.

Art and sound

  • Marc's art: a concept painting per hole, the seven balls (Jack, Boo, Bones, Wraps, The Count, Frankie, Batty), four pin flags (pumpkin, moon, skull, ghost), the hanging-pumpkin lanterns, the golf bag, the chapel and house concepts, and the foliage packs.
  • The golfer: drawn frames cut from rendered video (driver, iron, putting, celebration), shown as a 2D figure in the 3D world.
  • Night look: a black sky with painted stars, clouds and a moon; deliberately dark ("slightly darker than the original" was Marc's call); a Brightness option for dim phone screens.
  • Music: three songs: "Brittany's Graveyard Shift", "Bad Luck on the Back Nine" and "Stay Off the Grass".
  • Sound: chalk and eraser, swing and landing thumps, and real thunder (a free CC0 recording) after each lightning flash.

Painted props being considered for 3D

Some painted props could become 3D models. Simple shapes are easy; creatures and figures would look blocky, so they stay painted.

Landmarks

Big buildings are 3D models built in code from Marc's concept paintings, with their surfaces (stone blocks, slates, clapboards, leaves) drawn by a shader instead of shipped as pictures, so each costs only 20–50 KB to download. Built so far: the chapel (hole 3), the homecoming house (9), the barn and silo (5) and the vampire's mansion (7).

How it's built

  • Engine: Godot 4.5, exported to the web (WebGL 2, single-threaded), hosted on Vercel.
  • Holes: each hole starts as a layout file (fairway path, green, bunkers, water, zones, trees, features). A Python builder runs Blender headless to make the ground, its surfaces and models, and checks the slopes against golf limits. The layouts are generated from one course plan.
  • Ball physics: its own simulation with carry tuned per club, wind, spin, bounce and roll by surface, and a forgiving cup.
  • Drawing: painted cards for plants (thousands per hole, drawn in about 20 batches), 3D for the ground, buildings, pumpkins and gravestones. Pumpkins are stored once and copied into place.
  • Smoothness: before each hole everything is drawn once behind a loading card, so nothing is prepared mid-swing. On the web the 3D view adapts its sharpness to the phone's frame rate (85/75/65/55%).
  • Tests: a physics test suite, a bot that plays all nine holes and screenshots each stage, same-spot before/after screenshots, and browser tests on a throttled connection.

Size and loading

The game downloads in stages: the title first, then the essentials while you're on the title, then each hole as the round reaches it, so you can start playing long before everything has arrived.

Download (phone)WhenSize
Engine + titleBefore the title shows≈ 11.5 MB
Core: her frames, bag, lanterns, first songBehind the title (PLAY waits)10.6 MB
Course: ground textures, sky, shared plantsBehind the clubhouse6.0 MB
Each holeBefore that hole (the next is fetched ahead)1.2–3.0 MB + shared pictures
Whole round≈ 61 MB

A download audit this week cut a full round from about 105 MB to about 61 MB, with no visible change: pumpkins stored once, no picture downloaded twice, no unused copies of the ground, smaller ball pictures, and textures downloaded only for holes that use them.

Known quirks

  • Hole 2's pool is hard to see from the low tee camera.
  • The 3 wood gets picked for many 150–180 yard shots (the 10%-to-spare rule).
  • Hole 3's flyover feels fast (it takes the same 5 seconds on every hole).
  • On mobile data (not Wi-Fi), background downloads during play may cost some smoothness.

How the work is done

  • Marc reviews before anything goes on the course: previews beside his concept art first.
  • Real screenshots are checked before anything is called done; tests and the bot round before every deploy.
  • Production deploys only when Marc asks; licences of any outside asset are checked first.
